elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay liquidated damages or other liquidated amounts.
elements.evidence: The added provision expressly requires PB to pay a “single early-termination fee” and characterizes that fee as “a liquidated amount.”

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay penalties.
elements.evidence: The provision does not prohibit Customer-payable penalties and retains a termination-triggered charge that may operate as a penalty, notwithstanding its “fee” label.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer is payable only as a single early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The provision supersedes each Development-Cost-based amount under Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10, including interest and amounts labeled as Trial Data Package consideration, and makes them payable “solely as a single early-termination fee.”

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at an amount equal to three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The operative cap is three times the average monthly “Development Costs paid or incurred” by SFJ during the preceding 12 months. Development Costs are not stated to be fees, so this does not demonstrably impose the required three-month-fees cap.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The provision expressly states that the fee “is the sole liquidated amount payable by PB under this Agreement.”

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because it retains a Customer-payable liquidated amount. It also falls short of the fallback because its cap uses average monthly Development Costs rather than three months' fees. The broad superseding and sole-liquidated-amount language otherwise effectively consolidates the identified termination payments without displacing unrelated Approval Payments, but the cap metric is materially misaligned and the provision does not specify the actual fee amount below the ceiling.
